title: Labels.String() is slow and allocation-heavy because it grows a heap bytes.Buffer and allocates a fresh quoted string per label value

source.license_note: Real upstream prometheus optimization PR #13673; measured-speedup task.

task.summary: Speed up Labels.String() so it stops allocating a heap-growing buffer and a fresh quoted string for every label value, without changing the rendered output.
task.instructions: Optimize the model/labels package for speed WITHOUT changing behavior. The benchmark BenchmarkString measures it; existing tests must still pass.
task.acceptance_notes: Behavior preserved (go test passes); higher measured speedup is better. Do NOT edit any *_test.go.

code_fault.description: Labels.String() allocates a heap-growing bytes.Buffer and calls strconv.Quote per label, producing a fresh quoted string allocation for every value on a hot serialization path.

ops_fault.description: CPU/alloc profile of label-set serialization shows bytes.Buffer growth and per-label strconv.Quote string allocations dominating Labels.String() in model/labels/labels_common.go.
detection_keywords: GC pressure from per-label quoted strings
heap bytes.Buffer growth in hot loop

visible_context.issue_text: Serializing a Labels set to its text form via Labels.String() is unexpectedly slow and allocation-heavy, showing up in CPU and allocation profiles wherever label sets are formatted for logs, errors, or output.
error_logs: pprof: 38.7% cpu/alloc in model/labels.Labels.String -> strconv.Quote + bytes.(*Buffer).grow; BenchmarkString ~520 ns/op, 11 allocs/op
visible_context.notes: Real upstream optimization; profiling diagnosis injected as upstream context.
